Action Plan:
1. Urgent clinic appointment to be arranged so the patient can be assessed for dehydration and a stool sample can be collected and submitted for testing (clinic to send sample same day rather than by post).
2. Obtain stool sample at clinic for testing to rule out bacterial gastroenteritis.
3. Clinical assessment of hydration status in clinic; if patient becomes more unwell or cannot keep fluids, advise immediate attendance at Emergency Department (A&E).
4. Home management advice provided: continue oral rehydration solution (ORS) in very small, frequent sips; avoid fruit, raw vegetables, and milk; eat simple bland foods if tolerated (e.g., toast or biscuits).
5. If stool testing identifies a bacterial cause, targeted antimicrobial treatment may be prescribed (no antibiotic prescribed at this consult).
6. Book appointment through the support line as discussed; patient to re-contact if symptoms worsen before appointment.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of diarrhea and vomiting.
- Diarrhea: started watery then very loose; at least 4 episodes today; no blood noted.
- Vomiting: ongoing, unable to keep liquids down; last vomiting episode this morning ~2 hours prior to consult.
- Fever: subjective high temperature ("literally boiling"); no thermometer reading available.
- Abdominal pain: periumbilical (central, around the navel), tender to touch, intermittent cramping associated with urgent need to defecate.
- Urination: passed urine about 1 hour before consult; able to urinate.
- Exposure: brother with similar symptoms; possible household/ school outbreak.
- Past medical history: none reported (no chronic conditions disclosed); occasional menstrual cramps.
- Surgeries: none reported.
- Medications: vitamin D daily (dose not documented); ibuprofen PRN for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented). 
- Social history: lives with brother and mother; works as a graphics designer; working from home today; does not smoke; occasional alcohol ("a pint from time to time"); no recreational drug use reported.
- Contraception/sexual history: not on contraception; not sexually active currently. Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Allergies: not documented.

Objective:
- No formal vital signs documented.
- Abdomen: patient reports focal tenderness centrally at the navel (periumbilical); pain intermittent.
- Hydration indicators: patient reports vomiting and diarrhea but passed urine ~1 hour prior (suggesting some urine output).
- No visible rash reported.
- No blood observed in stool or urine per patient report.
- No investigations/results available at time of consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrheal illness / gastroenteritis:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis (condition name only).
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral gastroenteritis; bacterial gastroenteritis; foodborne illness.
   - Investigations planned: Stool sample for testing (to be collected at clinic and sent for analysis).
   - Treatment planned: Continue ORS in very small, frequent sips; dietary advice — simple bland foods if tolerated (toast/biscuits); avoid fruit, raw vegetables, and milk. No antibiotics prescribed at this visit; antibiotics may be considered if stool testing identifies a bacterial pathogen.
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent clinic appointment for sample collection and assessment.

2. Dehydration (risk from vomiting and diarrhea):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Dehydration (risk) (condition name only).
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A (risk related to ongoing GI losses).
   - Investigations planned: Clinical assessment of hydration in clinic (no specific blood tests documented in transcript).
   - Treatment planned: Reinforce frequent small sips of ORS; if unable to maintain oral intake or symptoms worsen, urgent transfer to A&E for further management.
   - Relevant referrals: Advice to attend A&E if more unwell or unable to keep fluids down; urgent clinic assessment arranged.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: measured vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate), weight, pregnancy status/urine pregnancy test (patient is of childbearing age and last period 2 weeks ago), allergy clarification, complete medication doses and frequencies, exact appointment time/confirmation, results of stool testing (pending).
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality: overall adequate. A few brief inaudible/paused segments early in the consult but key clinical information was clearly captured.
